threads.body: This relies on the `Test` task name (`name`) matching the test suite name exactly. With Gradle JVM test suites, per-target tasks can be generated with names that don’t equal the suite name (e.g., when multiple targets are used), causing `findByName(name)` to return null and the agent configuration to be applied even for `*unitTests` suites. Consider tagging/configuring the suite’s `targets.all { testTask.configure { ... } }` directly (or otherwise deriving the suite from the task in a way that doesn’t depend on exact name equality) so all tasks belonging to a `*unitTests` suite are consistently excluded.

The check is currently case-insensitive (`ignoreCase = true`). Gradle suite names are typically treated as case-sensitive identifiers, so this may unintentionally exclude suites with mixed-case suffixes. If the intent is specifically `...unitTests` as documented in the PR description, prefer a case-sensitive check (or document that casing is intentionally ignored).

replies.body: deliberately using case insensitive comparison so that both `unitTests` and `xxxUnitTest` would match
